cards.text: Right before this, the writer of Hebrews says Jesus was made like His brothers in every way, to become a merciful and faithful high priest (Hebrews 2:17). So now he writes to the ones he calls “holy brothers, who share in the heavenly calling,” and his ask is simple: “set your focus on Jesus, the apostle and high priest whom we confess.”
Eyes off the group chat, eyes off the bills, eyes on JESUS. And the writer says Jesus was faithful to the One who appointed Him.

cards.question: The writer compares Jesus to a famous name from Israel's history. Jesus was faithful to the One who appointed Him, just as ___ was faithful in all God's house.

cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, is such a BIG name that if Israel had a hall of fame, he'd get his own wing. But the writer says Jesus has been counted worthy of greater glory than Moses.

cards.question: To show that Jesus has greater glory than Moses, the writer uses a picture. What is it?

answers.text: A builder honored above the house
A shepherd honored above the sheep
A teacher honored above the student

cards.text: Nobody bites a cookie and says, “Forget the baker, give THIS cookie a trophy.” And the writer adds that every house is built by someone.

cards.question: True or false: The writer says every house is built by someone, but God is the builder of everything.

cards.text: Now back to Moses, who was faithful in all God's house, and nobody's taking that from him. But the writer gives him a certain role there.

cards.question: What was Moses' role in God's house? Moses was faithful as a ___ in all God's house.

cards.text: A faithful servant, testifying to what would be spoken later. That's an important job, and now the writer turns to Christ.

cards.question: Moses was faithful as a servant in God's house. How is Christ faithful?

answers.text: As the Son over God's house
As a guest inside God's house

cards.question: The writer keeps talking about God's house. Then he tells the holy brothers what God's house is. What does he say?

cards.text: Friend, I spent YEARS stuck in the back of a junk drawer, and here believers get to BE God's house. Talk about a promotion, but the writer hangs one small word on it: “if.”

cards.question: True or false: The writer says we are His house whether or not we hold firmly to our confidence and the hope of which we boast.

cards.text: Now the writer quotes words the Holy Spirit says, from Psalm 95 (Psalm 95:7-11). They start with a word you're going to hear again: “Today.”

cards.question: The Holy Spirit's words begin, “Today, if you hear His voice,” and then comes a warning. What does it warn against?

cards.text: The words point back to the rebellion, the day of testing in the wilderness. That's where the fathers tested and tried God.

cards.question: In the wilderness, the fathers tested and tried God. For how long did they see His works?

cards.text: That's like watching the oven turn out perfect cookies every single day for FORTY YEARS and still asking, “But are we SURE this thing gets hot?” So God was angry with that generation.

cards.question: True or false: God said that generation's hearts were finally starting to follow His ways.
God said their hearts were always going astray and they had not known His ways. So in His anger He swore an oath. What did He swear they would never enter?

cards.text: Now the writer turns from the wilderness to his own readers. And he gets personal: “See to it, brothers,”

cards.question: What kind of heart does the writer warn the brothers about?
A heart of unbelief turns away from the living God. So none of them gets hardened, what does the writer tell the brothers to do?

cards.text: DAILY, as long as it is called today. That's a group chat that actually checks on you, friend, not the one that's been dead quiet since somebody's birthday back in March.

cards.question: True or false: The writer warns that sin is deceitful and can harden a heart.

cards.text: Sin's deceitfulness works like the snooze button: “Just five more minutes,” and suddenly it's noon and NOBODY knows where the day went. Then the writer says we have come to share in Christ, and there's an if attached.

cards.question: We have come to share in Christ if we hold firmly to the assurance we had at first. For how long does the writer say to hold firmly?

cards.text: He quotes the Psalm again: “Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts, as you did in the rebellion.” Then he starts asking questions, like a baker checking every oven.

cards.question: The writer asks who heard and rebelled. His answer: all those ___ led out of Egypt.
The writer asks who God was angry with for forty years. His answer: those who sinned, whose bodies fell in the ___.
True or false: The writer says God swore that those who disobeyed would never enter His rest.
The writer sums it all up. It was because of their ___ that they were unable to enter.

findings.problem: The story card ends by saying the writer hangs "if" on being God's house. That tells the baker the promise is conditional, which gives away the answer to card 14. Card 14 asks whether we are His house "whether or not we hold firmly," and the answer is False. The setup should bring the baker to the condition without naming it.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.
